change: The gRPC shared benchmark now accepts --max-frame-size and applies it to both endpoints through http2.runtime.Limits. Result and peer-completion records include max_frame_size.
conclusions: Raising both HTTP/2 windows to 1 MiB and SETTINGS_MAX_FRAME_SIZE to 64 KiB improves netz-to-netz 256-KiB persistent gRPC by about 4.7% mean and 4.0% p50, with 3/3 paired wins.

The earlier window-only capture measured a single default-window run at about 836 us; the current 1-MiB/16-KiB run is about 741 us, so window tuning now matters more than the earlier 0-4% observation.
This tuning cannot close the grpc-cpp comparison by itself: grpc-cpp advertises its own 16-KiB maximum frame size and window policy, and the cross-stack fixture must keep its peer settings.
The benchmark option is a reproducible tuning path for deployments where both endpoints are netz and can adopt the larger frame size.
